overview: Two common refractive errors of the eye, differing in where light rays focus relative to the retina and which corrective lens fixes them.
genZNote: Myopia: distant things look blurry, close things are fine. Hypermetropia: the opposite problem entirely.

aspects.label: Common Structural Cause
aspects.valueA: Elongated eyeball, or excessive curvature of the cornea/lens.
aspects.valueB: Shortened eyeball, or insufficiently curved cornea/lens.

aspects.label: Vision Affected
aspects.valueA: Distant objects appear blurry; near vision is normal.
aspects.valueB: Near objects appear blurry; distant vision is normal.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens, hypermetropia with a convex lens — a very frequently tested pairing with ray diagrams.
overlay.memoryTrick: Myopia = 'my-oh-so-close', can't see far. Hypermetropia = can't see stuff that's near.
overlay.commonMisconception: Presbyopia (age-related loss of near focus, due to lens stiffening) is a separate condition from hypermetropia, even though both make near objects hard to see.
